title: Linear remaining quantity at a constant rate
microskill_statement: From two snapshots of a quantity changing at a constant rate, find the rate, then use Q(t) = Q0 − r t to solve for time or remaining amount.
review_gate: No item may enter a scored precheck, independent, transfer, or delayed slot until status is teacher_approved.

items.role: Untimed first attempt. Do not label the student as can/cannot. Record first answer, hint use, and time.
items.stem_html: A warehouse starts with 15,600 pounds of grain. A conveyor removes grain at a constant rate. After 4 hours, 13,000 pounds remain. If the conveyor continues at this rate, what is the total number of hours from the start until 7,800 pounds remain?

worked_steps.do: Grain removed in the first 4 hours: 15,600 − 13,000 = 2,600 pounds.
worked_steps.why: At a snapshot, remaining = start − removed, so removed is the difference.

worked_steps.do: Constant rate r = 2,600 ÷ 4 = 650 pounds per hour.
worked_steps.why: Constant rate means the same amount is removed in every hour, so rate = removed ÷ elapsed time.

worked_steps.do: To leave 7,800 pounds, the conveyor must remove 15,600 − 7,800 = 7,800 pounds from the original pile.
worked_steps.why: The unknown is total time from the same start as the 4-hour snapshot, so the target remaining is measured from Q0, not from the 13,000-pound snapshot.
Time = total amount removed from the start ÷ rate.

traps: 8 = (13,000 − 7,800)/650 without adding back the 4 hours if the question had asked additional hours — here the question asks total hours, and 4+8=12 still recovers C if done carefully
items.source_note: Original pilot item. Not copied from question_bank.json.
items.light_hint: Identify the constant rate from the two snapshots (start and after 4 hours). Do not compute the final time yet.
items.critical_hint: Grain dropped 2,600 pounds in 4 hours, so r = 650 per hour. The unknown is total time from the start until 7,800 remain, so set 15,600 − 650t = 7,800.
items.core_idea: A constant-rate remaining quantity follows Q(t) = Q0 − r t, with r from a snapshot pair.
items.common_mistake: Adding the opening 4 hours twice, or treating 7,800 as additional hours from the 13,000-pound snapshot without converting to total time.

items.stem_html: Maya pumps water from a tank at a constant rate. The tank held 8,400 gallons when she started. After 3 hours, 6,900 gallons remain. If she continues at this rate, how many total hours from the start will she have been pumping when 4,400 gallons remain?

worked_steps.why: Remaining is what is still in the tank, so the decrease is the amount removed.
The problem says the rate is constant, so this 3-hour average is the rate at every hour.

worked_steps.do: To leave 4,400 gallons, Maya must pump 8,400 − 4,400 = 4,000 gallons in total from the start.
worked_steps.why: Both snapshots are measured from the same starting amount, so the target is also from Q0.
Hours = gallons removed ÷ gallons per hour.

items.stem_html: A machine sands wood from a pile at a constant rate. The pile started at 2,400 kilograms. After 5 hours, 1,650 kilograms remain. How many total hours from the start until 600 kilograms remain?

given_steps.label: Given
given_steps.text: A machine sands wood from a pile at a constant rate. Start 2,400 kg; after 5 hours, 1,650 kg remain.

blanks.prompt: Total hours from the start until 600 kg remain: t = ___

worked_steps.why: Difference between start and the 5-hour remaining amount.
Constant rate = amount changed ÷ time for that change.

worked_steps.do: Need to sand 2,400 − 600 = 1,800 kg from the start.
worked_steps.why: Target remaining is 600 from the original 2,400.
Time = total change from start ÷ rate.

items.core_idea: Finish the faded steps: r = ΔQ / Δt, then t = (Q0 − Q_target) / r.

Time = total removed ÷ rate.

Hours = gallons ÷ (gallons per hour).

items.stem_html: A feed silo starts with 18,200 kilograms of grain. An unloader removes grain at a constant rate. After 5 hours, 15,450 kilograms remain. How many kilograms remain after the unloader has run for 12 hours from the start?

worked_steps.why: Same remaining-difference step as before.
Constant rate.

worked_steps.do: The question asks for remaining at t = 12, not for the time when remaining hits a target.
worked_steps.why: The unknown changed from t to Q(t). The model is still Q(t) = Q0 − r t.
Substitute the given time into the linear remaining formula.

items.explanation_check: At t=5: 18,200 − 550×5 = 15,450, matching the given snapshot.
items.source_note: Original pilot item. Not copied from question_bank.json.
items.light_hint: The unknown is no longer a time. Ask what quantity the last sentence wants.
items.critical_hint: Rate is still (18,200 − 15,450)/5. The question asks for remaining at t = 12, so compute Q(12) = 18,200 − r·12.
items.core_idea: Same linear remaining model; the unknown switched from t to Q(t).
items.common_mistake: Solving for the time when remaining hits 12, or subtracting 12 hours from the 5-hour snapshot without using Q0 − r t.

items.stem_html: A storage yard holds 20,000 tons of gravel. Trucks remove gravel at a constant rate. After 7 hours, 16,500 tons remain. How many additional hours from that moment are needed until 9,500 tons remain?

worked_steps.why: Find the constant rate from the opening interval.
Constant rate.

worked_steps.do: From the 16,500-ton snapshot down to 9,500 tons is 7,000 tons still to remove.
worked_steps.why: The question asks for additional hours after hour 7, so the remaining drop starts at 16,500, not at 20,000.
Δt = ΔQ ÷ r from the current amount. Total time from the start would be 21, which is a different question.

traps: 21 = (20,000 − 9,500)/500, which is total hours from the start, not additional hours
items.explanation_check: After 7+14=21 hours from start: 20,000 − 500×21 = 9,500, so 14 more hours after the snapshot is correct.

items.critical_hint: r = 3,500/7 = 500 tons/h. From 16,500 down to 9,500 is 7,000 tons still to remove after hour 7.
items.core_idea: Additional time uses the current remaining amount, not Q0.
items.common_mistake: 21 = (20,000 − 9,500)/500, which is total hours from the start, not additional hours.

items.stem_html:
A hopper loses material at a constant rate. Remaining mass is recorded in the table.

Hours tRemaining mass R (kg)
09,600
48,000

Which function gives the remaining mass after t hours?

worked_steps.do: From t = 0 to t = 4, remaining falls 9,600 − 8,000 = 1,600 kg.
worked_steps.why: The table gives two snapshots of the same constant-rate process.
Constant rate is the slope of remaining versus time.

worked_steps.do: The unknown is the function R(t) from the t = 0 row, not a later remaining amount or a time.
worked_steps.why: A table-to-function transfer keeps Q(t) = Q0 − r t but changes how the data is presented.

worked_steps.do: R(t) = 9,600 − 400t. Check: R(4) = 9,600 − 1,600 = 8,000, matching the table.
worked_steps.why: Q0 is the t = 0 remaining mass, not the t = 4 value.

traps: R(t) = 8,000 − 400t uses the later snapshot as Q0
R(t) = 9,600 − 4t treats elapsed hours as the rate
R(t) = 400t − 9,600 has the wrong sign for remaining
items.explanation_check: R(4) = 9,600 − 400×4 = 8,000, which matches the table row for t = 4.
items.light_hint: The table is two snapshots. Read the slope (change in remaining per hour) before writing a formula.
items.critical_hint: Remaining drops 1,600 kg in 4 hours, so the slope is −400. The intercept must be the t = 0 remaining mass 9,600, not 8,000.
items.core_idea: The same linear remaining model can be encoded as a table or as a function R(t) = R(0) − r t.
items.common_mistake: Using the t = 4 remaining mass as the intercept, which gives R(t) = 8,000 − 400t.
items.unknown_change: The representation changed from a prose remaining-quantity story to a table, and the unknown is the function R(t) rather than a single time or remaining amount.
items.source_note: Original table-to-function transfer item. Not copied from question_bank.json.
